daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) detained a former tax official suspected of receiving Rp 20.7 billion in gratuities, a year after naming him a suspect. The KPK also rebutted Religious Affairs Minister Yaqut, claiming it can prove state losses in the hajj quota corruption case. In a separate immigration case, the KPK scheduled questioning of foreign nationals and uncovered alleged corruption involving foreign workers' BPJS during its investigation of residence permit extortion.

  • A DPR member sharply criticized the Director General of Sea Transportation over recurring ship accidents.
  • A DPR member called on Minister Purbaya to immediately disburse the budget for forest and land fire handling.
  • Jakarta Governor Pramono said Jakarta cannot be built alone and needs support from AHY's Democratic Party.
  • Democratic Party chairman AHY reminded party cadres to maintain peace and oversee post-disaster rehabilitation in Aceh.
  • The Attorney General's Office questioned nine forestry ministry employees related to the PT TPL transfer pricing case.
  • The Attorney General's Office examined six private-sector witnesses in the money laundering case against Febrie Adriansyah.
  • A court hearing in the Customs gratuities case was postponed two weeks due to the judge's busy schedule.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Defence Minister signaled Indonesia will receive additional fighter jets in future procurement. Separately, the Indonesian ambassador said cooperation with India has intensified following Prime Minister Modi's visit.

  • Development and modernization were the main agenda at a meeting between Indonesia's and China's foreign ministers.
  • Germany reaffirmed support for Indonesia's energy transition during a ministerial visit.
  • The TNI Army deployed 2,253 personnel to assist earthquake response efforts in East Nusa Tenggara.
  • The TNI Army dispatched a hospital ship to NTT carrying doctors and nurses.

Other

Indonesia proposed higher hajj pilgrimage costs for 2027 due to oil price increases and rupiah weakness. The Ministry of Religious Affairs said two of its offices in NTT were damaged by the earthquake, with staff and pilgrim safety now the priority. The National Disaster Agency (BNPB) reported 71 deaths from the NTT earthquake as relief efforts continue.

  • BMKG predicted aftershocks will continue in Flores for 21 to 30 days following the main quake.
  • The search for victims of the Putri Yasmin ferry fire officially ended after eight days.
  • Bank Indonesia said economic growth is well-maintained despite global uncertainty.
  • The government secured land and reservoirs for 30-gigawatt solar power development, with tenders starting this year.
  • SEFAS Group, owned by a pastor, acquired all Shell fuel stations in Indonesia.
